take.en: Run frontier-scale MoE models on a gaming PC — edge-native serving with agent-aware cache so tool edits do not recompute the whole context.

why.en: Coding agents burn tokens rewriting long contexts after every tool call. FreeToken is built for that loop: it serves huge open MoE weights on consumer GPUs and keeps semantic checkpoints so agentic edits can reuse work instead of restarting the prefill tax.

explanation.en: FreeToken is an open edge MoE engine from FlashML aimed at 290B+ class models on laptops and gaming desktops. It treats GPU, CPU, and host memory as one elastic pool, streams experts with bandwidth-adaptive co-execution, and exposes Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible APIs so tools like Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode can point at your machine. There is a desktop app plus a CLI, and a 2026 paper on the runtime design.

howItWorks.en: Install the desktop build from flashml.ai or `uv pip install "freetoken[accel]"`, load a supported MoE checkpoint (DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM and friends across MXFP4/NVFP4/FP8/BF16), and hit the local OpenAI- or Anthropic-shaped endpoint from your agent. Expert caches and KV memory can rebalance at runtime without a full reload; semantic anchor checkpoints cut redundant recomputation when the agent mutates tool or thinking blocks mid-run.

different.en: Most local stacks stop at “fit the model.” FreeToken is a full MoE serving layer with elastic VRAM policy and caches tuned for agent turns, not just chat demos — so the win is interactive frontier weights on hardware you already own, wired to real coding agents.
